text: 15. The concept of 'Gender Budgeting'—where a specific proportion of the budget is earmarked explicitly for women's development and empowerment schemes—was formally introduced in India in which financial year?
explanation: Gender Budgeting was introduced in the Union Budget of India in 2005-06. It is not a separate budget, but an analytical tool to assess how much of the government's spending specifically benefits women.

text: 16. In the Union Budget 2026, the government launched 'Biopharma SHAKTI' with an outlay of ₹10,000 crores to make India a global biologics manufacturing hub. What does the 'S' and 'H' in SHAKTI stand for?
explanation: Biopharma SHAKTI stands for Strategy for Healthcare Advancement through Knowledge, Technology and Innovation. It has a massive outlay of ₹10,000 crores over 5 years.

text: 17. As part of the Biopharma SHAKTI strategy in Budget 2026, the government proposed the establishment of how many entirely NEW National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER)?
explanation: The Budget 2026 proposal included building a robust network by establishing 3 new NIPERs and upgrading 7 existing ones to boost R&D in pharmaceuticals.

text: 18. To dominate the global hardware supply chain, the Union Budget 2026 massively increased the financial outlay for the 'Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme' to:
explanation: Initially allocated a smaller amount, the Budget 2026 significantly increased the outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme to ₹40,000 crore.

text: 19. The Budget 2026 introduced the 'SME Growth Fund' designed to provide equity support to micro and small enterprises to create future 'Champions'. What is the exact corpus of this fund?
explanation: The government proposed a dedicated ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund in the 2026 budget to specifically bolster the MSME sector with equity support.

text: 20. To reduce reliance on imported containers for export logistics, Budget 2026 allocated ₹10,000 crore over a 5-year period for which specific scheme?
explanation: The 'Scheme for Container Manufacturing' was allocated ₹10,000 crore to create a globally competitive domestic ecosystem for shipping containers.

text: 21. Addressing climate change obligations, Budget 2026 proposed an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for scaling up CCUS technologies across heavy industries like steel and cement. CCUS stands for:
explanation: CCUS stands for Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage. It is a critical emission reduction technology that captures CO2 from large point sources like factories.

text: 22. The 'Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme' in Budget 2026 seeks to incentivize a modal shift of freight from rail and road to water. What is the explicit target share for inland waterways and coastal shipping by 2047?
explanation: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme aims to double the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from the current 6% to 12% by the year 2047.

text: 23. In a move to liberalize Foreign Exchange regulations, Budget 2026 increased the overall investment limit for all individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs) in the equity of listed Indian companies to:
explanation: Budget 2026 increased the individual PROI limit to 10%, and the overall aggregate limit for all PROIs in a listed Indian company was raised to 24%.

text: 24. Budget 2026 proposed a dedicated programme to achieve self-reliance and make two specific agricultural cash crops into premium global brands by the year 2030. Which two crops are these?
explanation: A dedicated programme was announced in Budget 2026 for Indian Cashew and Cocoa to make the country self-reliant in processing and to transform them into global brands by 2030.

text: 25. Which mineral-rich state is NOT included in the Budget 2026 initiative to establish dedicated 'Rare Earth Corridors'?
explanation: The Budget 2026 explicitly proposed the establishment of Rare Earth Corridors in the states of Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. Karnataka is excluded from this specific list.

text: 26. To provide predictability in international trade, Budget 2026 extended the validity period of advance rulings binding on Customs from 3 years to:
explanation: The validity period of an advance ruling (which gives certainty to importers regarding classification and duty) was extended from 3 years to 5 years.

text: 27. In the Direct Tax proposals of Budget 2026, the Tax Collection at Source (TCS) rate was rationalized to a uniform 2% for scrap, alcoholic liquor, and minerals. However, for Tendu leaves, the TCS rate was REDUCED to 2% from:
explanation: To reduce multiplicity of tax rates, Budget 2026 reduced the TCS rate on the sale of Tendu leaves from 5% down to 2%, bringing it in line with other commodities like scrap.

text: 28. To resolve double taxation issues, what relief was provided in Budget 2026 regarding dividends received by one cooperative society from another?

options.text: It is allowed as a deduction to the extent it is further distributed to its members.
It is taxed as short-term capital gains.
It is subject to an additional 5% surcharge.

explanation: Budget 2026 proposed to allow the inter-cooperative society dividend income as a deduction under the new tax regime, provided it is further distributed to the members.

text: 29. Budget 2026 announced the establishment of 'Hi-Tech Tool Rooms' as digitally enabled automated service bureaus to build capital goods capacity. Who is responsible for establishing these at 2 locations?
explanation: These Hi-Tech Tool Rooms will be established by CPSEs at 2 locations to design, test, and manufacture high-precision components domestically.

text: 30. The Union Budget 2026 announced the creation of 3 dedicated Chemical Parks. What operational model will be used for these parks?
explanation: The 3 dedicated Chemical Parks will be established via a challenge route utilizing a cluster-based plug-and-play model, providing readymade infrastructure for chemical manufacturers.

text: 31. To boost the efficiency of internal trade logistics, Budget 2026 proposed the operationalisation of 20 new National Waterways over the next 5 years. Which waterway will be the first to start under this scheme?
explanation: The development will commence with NW-5, which connects the mineral-rich areas of Talcher and Angul in Odisha to the ports of Paradeep and Dhamra.

text: 32. To address manufacturing disruptions, Budget 2026 introduced a one-time measure allowing Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to sell their goods to the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA). What condition applies to this?

options.text: Sales are duty-free but limited to 10% of output.
Sales are allowed at concessional rates of duty, limited to a prescribed proportion of their exports.
Sales require 50% GST and approval from the RBI.
Only IT software services are allowed to be sold.

explanation: Eligible manufacturing units in SEZs can sell to the DTA at concessional duty rates, but this is capped at a prescribed proportion of their actual exports, preventing dumping in the domestic market.

text: 33. In Budget 2026, the duty deferral period for Tier 2 and Tier 3 Authorised Economic Operators (AEOs) was enhanced to improve cash flows. It was increased from 15 days to:
explanation: To promote trust-based systems, the duty deferral period for compliant Tier 2 and Tier 3 AEOs was doubled to 30 days.

text: 34. The Union Budget 2026 proposed establishing a new Dedicated Freight Corridor to promote sustainable cargo movement. This corridor will connect:
explanation: The proposed Dedicated Freight Corridor will run from East to West, specifically connecting Dankuni in West Bengal to Surat in Gujarat.

text: 35. In order to increase the competitiveness of the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) in India, Budget 2026 increased the period of tax deduction under section 147 to:
explanation: The deduction period was enhanced to 20 consecutive years out of 25 years for units located in the IFSC, providing a massive long-term tax incentive.

text: 36. In the Union Budget 2026, the government proposed six key areas of intervention under its first 'kartavya' to accelerate economic growth. Which of the following is NOT one of those six areas?
explanation: The six intervention areas are: i) Scaling up manufacturing, ii) Rejuvenating legacy industrial sectors, iii) Creating “Champion MSMEs”, iv) Push to Infrastructure, v) Ensuring long-term energy security, and vi) Developing City Economic Regions.

text: 37. To strengthen domestic manufacturing of technologically advanced equipment like tunnel-boring machines and multi-story lifts, Budget 2026 introduced which of the following schemes?

options.text: Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE)
Make in India Heavy Machinery Act

explanation: The Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) was introduced to boost the manufacturing of high-value equipment like fire-fighting tools, lifts, and tunnel-boring machines.

text: 38. The Integrated Programme for the Textile Sector proposed in Budget 2026 consists of 5 sub-parts. Which sub-part specifically focuses on modernizing the textile skilling ecosystem through collaboration with industry and academic institutions?
explanation: Samarth 2.0 is the specific sub-part of the textile programme designed to modernize and upgrade the textile skilling ecosystem by collaborating with academic institutions and the industry.

text: 39. Under the 5-part Integrated Textile Programme of Budget 2026, what is the primary objective of the 'Tex-Eco Initiative'?

options.text: To provide capital support for machinery upgradation.
To promote globally competitive and sustainable textiles and apparels.
To achieve self-reliance in natural fibres like silk and jute.
To provide direct cash transfers to handloom weavers.

explanation: The Tex-Eco Initiative was specifically introduced to promote sustainable (eco-friendly) and globally competitive practices within the textile and apparel sector.

text: 40. In Budget 2026, to improve cost competitiveness and efficiency through infrastructure and technology upgradation, the government proposed a scheme to revive how many 'legacy industrial clusters'?
explanation: The Finance Minister proposed a dedicated scheme to rejuvenate and revive 200 legacy industrial clusters across the country to improve their efficiency.

text: 41. To promote environmentally sustainable movement of cargo, Budget 2026 announced the setting up of a ship repair ecosystem catering to inland waterways. At which two locations will this ecosystem be established?
explanation: To support the operationalization of the new National Waterways, the Budget proposed setting up a dedicated ship repair ecosystem catering to inland waterways at Varanasi and Patna.

text: 42. To enhance last-mile and remote connectivity and promote tourism, Budget 2026 introduced a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme to support the operations of which specific mode of transport?
explanation: The Budget 2026 introduced a Seaplane VGF Scheme to provide support for operations and give incentives to indigenize the manufacturing of seaplanes.

text: 43. For exporters of leather garments, synthetic footwear, and textile garments, Budget 2026 provided massive relief by extending the time period for the export of the final product. The period was extended from 6 months to:
explanation: To facilitate ease of doing business in labour-intensive sectors, the time period for the export of final products for leather and textile exporters was doubled from 6 months to 1 year.

text: 44. To support green energy transitions, Budget 2026 exempted the basic customs duty on the import of 'Sodium Antimonate'. What is this chemical primarily used to manufacture in this context?
explanation: The Finance Minister proposed to exempt the basic customs duty on the import of sodium antimonate specifically for its use in the manufacture of solar glass.

text: 45. To incentivize the domestic mining sector, Budget 2026 proposed that the expenditure incurred on prospecting and exploring critical minerals will be eligible for deduction under which specific section of the Income Tax Act?
explanation: To boost self-reliance in strategic sectors, the expenditure on prospecting and exploring critical minerals was made eligible for deduction as per the provisions of Section 51 of the Act.

text: 46. Sandalwood is closely linked to India’s social and cultural heritage. According to Budget 2026, the Central Government will partner with whom to promote focused cultivation and restore the Sandalwood ecosystem?
explanation: Budget 2026 announced that the Central Government will formally partner with State Governments to promote focused cultivation and post-harvest processing to restore the glory of the Indian Sandalwood ecosystem.

text: 47. Under the Customs facilitation measures of Budget 2026, how will export cargo belonging to regular importers with trusted longstanding supply chains be processed to minimize verification delays?

options.text: Using armed escorts provided by the CISF.
Through biometric scanning of the drivers.
Using electronic sealing to provide clearance directly from the factory premises to the ship.
By completely abolishing export duties on their goods.

explanation: Trusted importers recognized in the risk system will be allowed to use 'electronic sealing' for their export cargo, providing seamless clearance directly from the factory premises to the ship.

text: 48. According to the Customs Tariff notifications in Budget 2026, the basic customs duty exemption on 'Naphtha, for use in the manufacture of fertilisers' is scheduled to lapse with effect from which date?
explanation: The Budget 2026 documents clearly list that the notification providing exemptions for items like Naphtha (for fertilisers) and Silicon (for solar cells) is set to lapse with effect from 01.04.2026.

text: 49. In economic taxation theory, what is an 'Ad Valorem' tax?

options.text: A fixed tax applied uniformly per unit of weight or volume, regardless of the item's price.
A tax based on the assessed value of an item, such as a percentage of a property's price.
A tax specifically levied on environmentally harmful goods.
A direct tax imposed only on corporate profits.

explanation: An Ad Valorem (Latin for 'according to value') tax is a tax whose amount is based on the value of a transaction or property. Examples include GST, VAT, and property taxes (e.g., 18% of the price).

text: 50. Conversely, a 'Specific Tax' (or specific duty) is strictly defined as:

options.text: A tax calculated as a fixed amount per physical unit of the good (e.g., per liter or per kg), regardless of its market price.
A tax levied exclusively on imported luxury goods.
A tax that increases as the income of the taxpayer increases.
A tax levied only on specified agricultural products.

explanation: A specific tax is a fixed fee levied on a particular quantity of a product (e.g., ₹10 per liter of petrol), completely independent of the product's fluctuating market value.

text: 51. Article 280 of the Indian Constitution mandates the formation of a Finance Commission every five years. What is its primary role in the context of the national budget?

options.text: To prepare the Annual Financial Statement.
To audit the accounts of the Government of India.
To recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
To set the Repo Rate and manage inflation.

explanation: The Finance Commission's core constitutional mandate is to recommend how the central government's tax revenues should be shared vertically (between the Centre and States) and horizontally (among different States).

text: 52. In the Union Budget, how is the 'Primary Deficit' precisely calculated?
explanation: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments on previous borrowings. It shows how much the government needs to borrow strictly to fund its current year's operations, without the burden of past debt.

text: 53. Which specific division of the Ministry of Finance is responsible for preparing and presenting the Union Budget to the Parliament?
explanation: The Budget Division under the Department of Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance) is the nodal agency responsible for the preparation of the Union Budget.

text: 54. What is the fundamental difference between a 'Cess' and a 'Surcharge' in the Indian taxation system?

options.text: A Cess is collected for a specific earmarked purpose, while a Surcharge is a general 'tax on tax' added to the consolidated fund.
A Surcharge is shared with the states, whereas a Cess is strictly retained by the Centre.
A Cess applies only to indirect taxes, while a Surcharge applies only to direct taxes.
A Surcharge is collected for a specific purpose (like health), while a Cess is for general use.

explanation: A Cess (like Education Cess) must be spent entirely on the purpose it was collected for. A Surcharge is simply an additional tax levied (usually on high-income brackets) that goes into the general revenue pool. Neither are shared with states.

text: 55. If the Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement) fails to be passed by the Lok Sabha, what is the constitutional consequence?

options.text: The budget is automatically sent to the President for emergency approval.
The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers must resign.
The Finance Minister is replaced, and the budget is presented again.
A joint sitting of Parliament is convened to pass it.

explanation: The passing of the budget is essentially a test of the government's majority. If the budget fails to pass in the Lok Sabha, it means the government has lost the confidence of the house, and the Prime Minister along with the council of ministers must resign.

text: 56. Which of the following government expenditures would be classified under 'Revenue Expenditure'?

options.text: Construction of a new National Highway.
Repayment of the principal amount of a World Bank loan.
Purchasing new fighter jets for the military.
Payment of salaries, pensions, and fertilizer subsidies.

explanation: Revenue Expenditure is day-to-day operational spending that neither creates an asset nor reduces a liability. Salaries, pensions, subsidies, and interest payments fall into this category. The other options are Capital Expenditures.

text: 57. In the Union Budget, 'Capital Receipts' are funds that either create a liability or cause a reduction in the government's assets. Which of the following is an example of a Capital Receipt?

options.text: Dividends and profits received from the RBI.
Money raised through the Disinvestment of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
Income generated from traffic fines and penalties.

explanation: Disinvestment involves the government selling its shares in a PSU, which reduces its assets. Therefore, the money received from this sale is classified as a Capital Receipt.

text: 58. What is the main objective of 'Performance Budgeting'?

options.text: To ensure that all previous year expenditures are strictly cut by 10%.
To link financial allocations to specific, measurable outcomes and physical targets.
To prepare the budget exclusively based on zero historical data.
To present the budget only for profit-making public enterprises.

explanation: Performance Budgeting shifts the focus from simply tracking how much money is spent (inputs) to tracking what is actually achieved with that money (outcomes and performance targets).

text: 59. The 'Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act' was enacted in 2003 to bring fiscal discipline to India. What does the 'M' in FRBM explicitly stand for?
explanation: FRBM stands for Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act. It sets targets to reduce the fiscal and revenue deficits over time.

text: 60. The phenomenon where high government borrowing (to finance a high fiscal deficit) drives up interest rates, thereby making it difficult for private businesses to borrow and invest, is called:
explanation: The 'Crowding Out Effect' occurs when massive government borrowing absorbs the available liquidity in the market, raising interest rates and 'crowding out' private sector investment.

text: 61. What does the macroeconomic term 'Fiscal Drag' describe?

options.text: When a government deliberately delays passing the budget.
When inflation naturally pushes taxpayers into higher income tax brackets without any real increase in their purchasing power.
When exports fall significantly below imports.
When the Central Bank refuses to change the repo rate during a recession.

explanation: Fiscal drag (or bracket creep) happens in a progressive tax system when inflation causes wages to rise nominally, pushing people into higher tax brackets. They pay more tax, even though their real purchasing power hasn't increased.

text: 62. The 'Twin Deficit' hypothesis refers to a situation where an economy suffers simultaneously from a high Fiscal Deficit and a high:
explanation: The Twin Deficit hypothesis refers to an economy facing both a high Fiscal Deficit (government overspending) and a high Current Account Deficit (country importing more than it exports).

text: 63. Which economic curve graphically illustrates the theoretical relationship between rates of taxation and the resulting levels of government tax revenue?
explanation: The Laffer Curve shows that starting from 0%, increasing tax rates will initially increase revenue. However, beyond a certain optimal point, higher tax rates discourage work and investment, thereby reducing total tax revenue collected.

text: 64. Progressive taxation, where the tax rate increases as the taxpayer's income increases, is primarily used by governments to achieve which socio-economic objective?

options.text: To reduce income inequality (Redistribution of wealth).
To maximize the Crowding Out effect.

explanation: By taxing higher-income earners at a higher percentage, the government redistributes wealth and reduces income inequality within the economy.

text: 65. If a government calculates its 'Revenue Deficit' and then subtracts the 'Grants in Aid for creation of capital assets', which specific deficit measure does it arrive at?
explanation: The Effective Revenue Deficit was introduced to exclude those revenue expenditures that are given as grants to states but are actually used to create long-term capital assets (like building schools or roads).

text: 66. Under Article 116, the 'Vote on Account' allows the government to withdraw advance funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to cover routine expenses pending the passage of the budget. Typically, this covers the expenditure for how many months?
explanation: A Vote on Account is usually passed for a period of two months, generally representing one-sixth of the total estimated expenditure for the financial year.

text: 67. Which of the following is considered an 'Injection' into the macroeconomic Circular Flow of Income?
explanation: Injections are funds entering the economy that boost total spending. Investment, Government Spending, and Exports are injections. Savings, Taxes, and Imports are leakages.

text: 68. In macroeconomics, an 'Inflationary Gap' occurs under which of the following conditions?

options.text: When Aggregate Supply exceeds Aggregate Demand at full employment.
When Aggregate Demand exceeds Aggregate Supply at the level of full employment.
When the government achieves a surplus budget.
When foreign direct investment drops to zero.

explanation: An Inflationary Gap occurs when total demand exceeds the economy's maximum capacity to produce at full employment. Since output cannot increase further, the excess demand strictly pushes prices up.

text: 69. In a 2-Sector economic model consisting only of Households and Firms, macroeconomic equilibrium is reached when:
explanation: In a simple 2-sector closed economy, there is no government or foreign trade. Equilibrium occurs when the leakages equal the injections, which strictly means Savings (S) equals Investment (I).

text: 70. What is the exact formula for the Keynesian Investment Multiplier, assuming 'c' represents the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC)?
explanation: The Multiplier is calculated as 1 / (1 - MPC), or 1 / MPS. It shows how much total economic output increases with a new injection of investment.

text: 71. In consumer theory, what does a point completely *inside* (or below) the Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) represent?

options.text: Full and efficient utilization of resources.
Under-utilization or inefficient use of available resources.

explanation: A point inside the PPF means the economy is producing less than its maximum potential, indicating that resources are unemployed or being used inefficiently.

text: 72. What is the fundamental difference between an Indifference Curve (IC) and an Isoquant Curve?

options.text: An IC is upward sloping, while an Isoquant is downward sloping.
An IC represents equal consumer satisfaction, while an Isoquant represents combinations of inputs yielding equal firm output.
An IC measures inflation, while an Isoquant measures unemployment.
An IC deals with macroeconomics, while an Isoquant deals with taxation.

explanation: An Indifference Curve (IC) shows combinations of two goods that give a consumer equal utility (satisfaction). An Isoquant Curve shows combinations of inputs (like labor and capital) that produce the same quantity of output for a firm.

text: 73. In terms of economic goods classification, 'Public Goods' like National Defense and streetlights are defined by which two properties?
explanation: Public Goods are Non-Excludable (you cannot stop someone from using them) and Non-Rivalrous (one person's use does not diminish another's use). Because of this, they suffer from the 'Free Rider' problem.

text: 74. The 'Income Method' of calculating National Income sums up Compensation of Employees, Mixed Income, and 'Operating Surplus'. What does the Operating Surplus specifically consist of?
explanation: Operating Surplus (OS) is the sum of property and entrepreneurial income. It strictly consists of Rent, Interest, and Profit (Mnemonic: R.I.P).

text: 75. In the Expenditure Method formula for GDP [C + I + G + (X - M)], what does '(X - M)' represent?
explanation: In the Expenditure Method, X stands for Exports and M stands for Imports. Therefore, (X - M) represents Net Exports, showing the net spending by the foreign sector on domestic goods.

text: 1. According to recent SSC CGL exam analysis, which topic holds the highest weightage in the Economics section, accounting for nearly 47 questions in recent shifts?
explanation: Recent extensive analysis of TCS-conducted SSC CGL exams reveals that 'Industrial Policy' (along with Major Industries) is the most heavily tested topic in Economics, accounting for roughly 47 recent questions [1].

text: 2. After Independence, the Government of India announced its first Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) in which year?
explanation: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of India was announced on April 6, 1948, by then Industry Minister Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee.

text: 3. The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 officially laid the foundation for which type of economic system in India?
explanation: The IPR 1948 declared India to be a Mixed Economy, meaning both the public sector (government) and private sector would co-exist and contribute to industrial development.

text: 4. Which Industrial Policy is often referred to as the 'Economic Constitution of India' and formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan?
explanation: The IPR 1956, heavily influenced by the Mahalanobis model of prioritizing heavy industries, is known as the 'Economic Constitution of India'.

text:
5. Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully:
Assertion (A): The IPR 1956 created an industrial classification into Schedules A, B, and C.
Reason (R): This was to identify sectors for exclusive state control, joint sectors, and private sector operation.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: Both statements are correct. IPR 1956 systematically categorized industries into three schedules to demarcate the exact roles of the public and private sectors in India's industrialization [2].

text: 6. Under Schedule A of the Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956, how many industries were designated as an exclusive monopoly of the State (Central Government)?
explanation: Schedule A consisted of 17 key heavy and strategic industries (e.g., arms, atomic energy, iron and steel, railways) that were exclusively reserved for the public sector.

text: 7. Under Schedule B of the IPR 1956, how many industries were listed where the State would increasingly establish new units, but private enterprises were expected to supplement the effort?
explanation: Schedule B contained 12 industries (such as machine tools, fertilizers, and road/sea transport) forming the 'mixed sector' where both state and private enterprises operated, with the state taking the lead.

text: 8. How did the strict 'Licensing Policy' under the pre-1991 planning era negatively affect the emergence of a competitive industrial sector in India?

options.text: It increased foreign direct investment (FDI) uncontrollably.
It allowed established large firms to block competitors by hoarding licenses.
It enhanced rural employment at the cost of urban jobs.
It caused massive deflation in the market.

explanation: The 'License Raj' was highly restrictive. Big industrial conglomerates often secured manufacturing licenses not to start new production, but simply to hoard them, legally preventing new competitors from entering the market [3].

text: 9. In 1969, the Indian government enacted the MRTP Act to prevent the concentration of economic power in the hands of a few. What does MRTP stand for?
explanation: MRTP stands for Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, 1969. It subjected large companies (with assets above a certain threshold) to severe restrictions regarding expansion and mergers.

text: 10. In response to a severe Balance of Payments crisis, the landmark New Industrial Policy (New Economic Policy) was announced on July 24, 1991. Who was the Prime Minister of India at this time?
explanation: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister, and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister when the historic 1991 LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) reforms were introduced.

text:
11. Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The 1991 reforms boosted India's foreign exchange reserves significantly.
Reason (R): Liberalized trade policies increased both exports and capital inflows.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: Both statements are correct. The 1991 reforms removed harsh import/export restrictions and allowed Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), leading to a massive surge in India's depleted forex reserves [2].

text: 12. The 1991 Industrial Policy abolished industrial licensing for all but a short list of specific industries related to security and strategic concerns. Today, how many industries require compulsory licensing?
explanation: Currently, only 5 industries require compulsory licensing: 1) Alcoholic drinks, 2) Cigarettes/Tobacco, 3) Aerospace and Defense equipment, 4) Industrial explosives, and 5) Hazardous chemicals.

text: 13. While the 1956 policy reserved 17 industries for the public sector, the 1991 policy drastically reduced this number. Currently, how many industrial sectors are exclusively reserved for the State?
explanation: Currently, only 2 sectors are strictly reserved for the Central Government: Atomic Energy and specific Railway Operations (though certain railway areas are now seeing private participation).

text: 14. Under the New Economic Policy of 1991, the draconian MRTP Act was eventually repealed and replaced by a modern law focused on promoting fair market rivalry. What is the name of this new act?
explanation: The MRTP Act was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which established the Competition Commission of India (CCI) to prevent anti-competitive agreements and monopolies.

text: 15. In terms of Indian Industrial Policy, 'Privatization through Disinvestment' strictly refers to:

options.text: The complete closure of bankrupt public enterprises.
Selling a part of government equity (shares) in Public Sector Undertakings to public or private entities.
Merging multiple private sector companies into one.
Issuing sovereign bonds to private foreign investors.

explanation: Disinvestment is the process where the government sells a portion of its ownership (equity) in a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) to private investors or the general public to raise revenue and increase efficiency [3].

text: 16. To facilitate a robust manufacturing ecosystem, the Indian government revised the definition of MSMEs in 2020. Under the new composite criteria, a 'Micro' enterprise must have an investment in plant and machinery not exceeding:
explanation: Under the revised 2020 MSME classification (which removed the distinction between manufacturing and services), a Micro enterprise is one where investment does not exceed ₹1 Crore and annual turnover does not exceed ₹5 Crore.

text: 17. According to the 2020 MSME revised definitions, what is the maximum annual turnover limit for an enterprise to be classified as a 'Small' enterprise?
explanation: For a 'Small' enterprise, the investment limit is up to ₹10 Crore and the annual turnover limit is up to ₹50 Crore.

text: 18. What is the investment and turnover threshold for an enterprise to be officially classified as a 'Medium' enterprise in India?

options.text: Investment up to ₹20 Cr, Turnover up to ₹100 Cr
Investment up to ₹50 Cr, Turnover up to ₹250 Cr
Investment up to ₹100 Cr, Turnover up to ₹500 Cr
Investment up to ₹10 Cr, Turnover up to ₹50 Cr

explanation: A 'Medium' enterprise is defined as having an investment in plant and machinery up to ₹50 Crore, and an annual turnover not exceeding ₹250 Crore.

text:
19. Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Globalization has led to increased outsourcing of services to India.
Reason (R): India offers high-cost, low-skill services to foreign companies.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: Assertion (A) is true; globalization made India an IT and BPO outsourcing hub. However, Reason (R) is completely false. Outsourcing boomed because India offers low-cost, high-skill (especially English-speaking) labor [4].

text: 20. The 'Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme' has been introduced for various industrial sectors in India. What is the primary goal behind the implementation of this scheme?

options.text: To nationalize failing private sector manufacturing units.
To reduce India's import dependence and boost domestic manufacturing by offering financial incentives on incremental sales.
To provide universal basic income to industrial workers.
To completely ban all imports from neighboring countries.

explanation: The PLI scheme aims to make Indian manufacturers globally competitive, attract investment in core sectors, and significantly reduce import bills by providing companies cash incentives based on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India [5].

text: 21. To grant greater operational and financial autonomy to high-performing Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), the government introduced the 'Maharatna' status in which year?
explanation: The 'Maharatna' scheme was introduced in 2010 for top-tier CPSEs to empower them to expand operations and emerge as global giants. (Navratna and Miniratna were introduced earlier in 1997).

text: 22. Which of the following is a mandatory financial prerequisite for a CPSE to be granted the elite 'Maharatna' status?

options.text: Average annual turnover of more than ₹10,000 crore during the last 3 years.
Average annual net profit after tax of more than ₹5,000 crore during the last 3 years.
Average annual net worth of more than ₹50,000 crore during the last 3 years.
The company must be 100% owned by the government with no private shares.

explanation: To become a Maharatna, a CPSE must already have Navratna status, be listed on the Indian stock exchange, have an average annual turnover > ₹25,000 cr, average net worth > ₹15,000 cr, and an average net profit > ₹5,000 cr during the last 3 years.

text: 23. In 1987, the Government of India set up the BIFR to detect 'sick' industrial companies and assist in their revival or closure. What does BIFR stand for?

options.text: Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
Bank for Industrial Funding and Recovery

explanation: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was an agency established under the Sick Industrial Companies Act (SICA) of 1985 to rehabilitate struggling industries. It was dissolved in 2016 and replaced by the NCLT.

text:
24. Read the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): Aluminium smelting is the most important metallurgical industry in India.
Reason (R): Aluminium is used in the manufacture of aircraft, wires, and utensils.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are false

explanation: Assertion (A) is false because Iron and Steel is the most important metallurgical industry in India, not Aluminium. However, Reason (R) is true as Aluminium's light weight and conductivity make it essential for aircraft, wires, and utensils [6].

text: 25. Which industrial sector is universally recognized as the oldest and largest organized large-scale industry in India, heavily contributing to employment?
explanation: The Cotton Textile industry is the oldest and one of the largest organized sectors in India. The first successful modern textile mill was established in Mumbai in 1854.

text: 26. During the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), heavily influenced by the Mahalanobis strategy, three major integrated iron and steel plants were set up in India. Which of the following pairs of 'Plant - Foreign Collaborator' is correctly matched?
explanation: Rourkela (Odisha) was set up with German help. Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) was set up with USSR (Russian) help. Durgapur (West Bengal) was set up with United Kingdom (British) help. Bokaro was established later during the 3rd FYP, also with USSR assistance.

text: 27. To promote exports, the Government of India enacted the Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act. In which year was this crucial industrial legislation passed by the Parliament?
explanation: The SEZ Act was passed by Parliament in May 2005 and came into effect in February 2006. It aimed to provide a hassle-free operational regime and tax holidays to boost export-oriented manufacturing.

text: 28. Long before the SEZ Act of 2005, India became the first country in Asia to set up an Export Processing Zone (EPZ). Where and when was this first EPZ established?
explanation: Recognizing the need to earn foreign exchange, Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) was established in Kandla, Gujarat, in 1965.

text: 29. As part of the globalization reforms, the draconian Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) of 1973 was repealed because it treated forex violations as criminal offenses. It was replaced by a more liberal act known as:
explanation: FERA was replaced by the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) in 1999. FEMA treated foreign exchange offenses as civil rather than criminal matters, facilitating easier external trade and payments.

text: 30. The 'National Manufacturing Policy' (NMP) introduced in 2011 aimed to increase the share of manufacturing in GDP to 25% within a decade. A key instrument of this policy was the creation of mega industrial zones called:
explanation: NIMZs were conceptualized under the National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) 2011. Unlike SEZs, which focus purely on exports, NIMZs are massive integrated industrial townships aimed at overall manufacturing growth.

text: 31. The 'Make in India' initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to transform India into a global design and manufacturing hub. In which year was this flagship industrial program launched?
explanation: The 'Make in India' initiative was officially launched on September 25, 2014, with the objective of facilitating investment, fostering innovation, and building best-in-class manufacturing infrastructure.

text: 32. The historic Iron and Steel plant at Jamshedpur (TISCO) was established by Jamshetji Tata. In which year was this pioneering private sector industrial venture founded?
explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 at Sakchi (later renamed Jamshedpur) in Jharkhand, marking the true beginning of India's modern iron and steel industry.

text: 33. Before 1991, India's industrial sector suffered from 'Tariff Jumping' FDI. Under the 1991 reforms, the government established the FIPB to drastically smoothen the approval of foreign investments. What does FIPB stand for?

options.text: Fund for Industrial Progress and Backing

explanation: The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) was a national agency offering single-window clearance for FDI proposals that did not fall under the automatic route. (It was officially abolished in 2017 to further streamline FDI).

text: 34. The concept of a 'Joint Sector' in Indian industries, which combines state financial capital with private sector management expertise, was strongly recommended by which historic committee?

options.text: Dutt Committee (Industrial Licensing Policy Inquiry Committee, 1969)

explanation: The Dutt Committee (1969) officially recommended the concept of the 'Joint Sector', where both public and private sectors would jointly establish and manage enterprises to curb monopolies and ensure social objectives.

text: 35. In modern industrial contexts, 'FDI' is preferred over 'FPI' for long-term economic growth. What fundamentally distinguishes Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) from Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI)?

options.text: FDI involves buying government bonds, while FPI involves buying private debt.
FPI brings in technology and management control, whereas FDI only brings capital.
FDI involves a lasting interest and control in a physical enterprise, while FPI involves short-term speculative buying of stocks and shares.
FDI is strictly restricted to the agricultural sector.

explanation: FDI involves establishing a direct business interest (like setting up a factory or buying a controlling stake in a company) bringing technology and stability. FPI refers to buying easily tradable financial assets (stocks/bonds) and is highly volatile ('hot money').

text: 36. While the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measure inflation and prices, which statistical indicator is used to measure the volume and growth of industrial production in India?
explanation: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measures the growth or volume of industrial production (Manufacturing, Mining, Electricity) over a specific period, acting as a gauge for the health of the industrial sector.

text: 37. Which government body is officially responsible for compiling and publishing the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India?

options.text: Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP)

explanation: The IIP is published by the National Statistical Organisation (NSO), which operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

text: 38. What is the current 'Base Year' utilized for calculating the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India?
explanation: The current base year for calculating the IIP is 2011-2012, though discussions are ongoing to update it to a more recent year like 2022-23.

text: 39. Established in 1955, the Karve Committee played a foundational role in India's industrial planning. What was the primary focus of this committee?
explanation: The Karve Committee (1955) was set up to promote rural development and employment through village and small-scale industries alongside the heavy industrialization of the Second Five-Year Plan.

text: 40. In standard economic development models, a country usually transitions from the Primary sector to the Secondary sector, and finally to the Tertiary sector. What was unique about India's developmental path?

options.text: India remained entirely in the Primary sector.
India jumped directly to the Tertiary (service) sector, skipping a strong, full industrialization phase (Secondary sector).
India developed the Secondary sector completely before moving back to the Primary sector.
India skipped the Primary sector entirely.

explanation: Unlike industrialized nations like China, India's economy uniquely leaped from an agrarian base directly to a service-oriented economy, largely skipping widespread industrialization and the robust development of the Secondary Sector.

text: 41. Workers engaged in the Secondary Sector, which involves transforming raw materials into valuable manufactured products, are conventionally classified as:
explanation: The Secondary Sector includes manufacturing, construction, and processing. Workers in these heavy labor and factory environments are traditionally referred to as 'Blue Collar' workers.

text: 42. The e-Shram portal was launched by the Indian Government to create a comprehensive national database of which specific demographic?
explanation: The e-Shram portal is a major initiative aimed at registering and securing the welfare of unorganized sector workers (like construction workers, street vendors, and domestic helpers) across India.

text: 43. Which of the following is NOT recognized as a Major Industrial Region in India?
explanation: The Major Industrial Regions in India include the Mumbai-Pune belt, Hugli belt, Bangalore-Tamil Nadu belt, Gujarat region, Chota Nagpur plateau, Vishakhapatnam-Guntur belt, Gurgaon-Delhi-Meerut belt, and Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram. The Thar Desert Corridor is not one of them.

text: 44. To build upon the semiconductor sector capabilities, the Union Budget 2026 proposed launching 'ISM 2.0'. What does ISM stand for?
explanation: ISM stands for India Semiconductor Mission. Budget 2026 launched ISM 2.0 to produce equipment and materials and design full-stack Indian IP to fortify supply chains.

text: 45. To capitalize on the manufacturing momentum, Budget 2026 proposed increasing the financial outlay for the 'Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme' to:
explanation: Launched initially with ₹22,919 crore, the outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme was significantly increased to ₹40,000 crore in the 2026 Budget.

text: 46. The Union Budget 2026 proposed establishing dedicated 'Rare Earth Corridors' to promote mining and processing. Which state is NOT included in this specific plan?
explanation: The Budget explicitly identified Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu to establish dedicated Rare Earth Corridors. Karnataka is not part of this specific list.

text: 47. To reduce import dependency and boost domestic production, Budget 2026 proposed supporting States in establishing dedicated Chemical Parks through a plug-and-play model. How many such Chemical Parks are planned?
explanation: The 2026 Budget announced a scheme to support States in establishing exactly 3 dedicated Chemical Parks.

text: 48. Which new scheme was introduced in Budget 2026 to strengthen the domestic manufacturing of technologically advanced items like lifts, fire-fighting equipment, and tunnel-boring machines?

options.text: Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE)

explanation: The Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) was explicitly introduced to boost domestic manufacturing of high-value equipment like tunnel-boring machines and multi-story lifts.

text: 49. In order to create a globally competitive logistics ecosystem, Budget 2026 allocated ₹10,000 crore over a 5-year period for which specific manufacturing scheme?
explanation: A budgetary allocation of ₹10,000 crore over 5 years was proposed for the Scheme for Container Manufacturing.

text: 50. For the labour-intensive Textile Sector, Budget 2026 proposed an Integrated Programme. How many sub-parts does this overarching textile programme have?
explanation: The Integrated Programme for the Textile Sector consists of 5 sub-parts (National Fibre Scheme, Textile Expansion, Handloom programme, Tex-Eco Initiative, and Samarth 2.0).

text: 51. Under the 5-part Integrated Textile Programme of Budget 2026, which scheme aims for self-reliance in natural fibres (like silk and jute) and new-age fibres?
explanation: The National Fibre Scheme is designed specifically to ensure self-reliance in the production of natural, man-made, and new-age fibres.

text: 52. Which sub-part of the Budget 2026 Textile Programme specifically focuses on modernizing and upgrading the textile skilling ecosystem through collaboration with academic institutions?
explanation: Samarth 2.0 is the specific sub-part of the textile programme designed to modernize the textile skilling ecosystem in collaboration with industry and academia.

text: 53. In Budget 2026, to improve cost competitiveness and efficiency through infrastructure and technology upgradation, the government proposed a scheme to revive how many 'legacy industrial clusters'?
explanation: The government proposed to introduce a scheme aimed at rejuvenating and reviving 200 legacy industrial clusters.

text: 54. Recognising MSMEs as a vital engine of growth, Budget 2026 introduced an equity support initiative called the 'SME Growth Fund'. What is the dedicated corpus for this fund?
explanation: A dedicated ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund was introduced to provide equity support and create future 'Champions' out of micro and small enterprises.

text: 55. To promote environmentally sustainable movement of cargo, Budget 2026 proposed establishing a new Dedicated Freight Corridor connecting which two major locations?

options.text: Dankuni in the East, to Surat in the West

explanation: Budget 2026 explicitly proposed the establishment of a new Dedicated Freight Corridor connecting Dankuni in the East to Surat in the West.

text: 56. The 'Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme' launched in Budget 2026 aims to incentivize a modal shift from rail and road to inland waterways. What is the target percentage share for coastal shipping by the year 2047?
explanation: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme targets increasing the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping in logistics from the current 6% to 12% by the year 2047.

text: 57. To address global trade disruptions affecting manufacturing units in Special Economic Zones (SEZs), Budget 2026 introduced a one-time measure allowing them to sell goods to which area at concessional duty rates?
explanation: As a special one-time measure, Budget 2026 allowed eligible manufacturing units in SEZs to sell goods to the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) at concessional rates of duty, limited to a prescribed proportion of their exports.

text: 58. According to the Customs Tariff notifications in Budget 2026, the basic customs duty exemption on 'Naphtha, for use in the manufacture of fertilisers' is scheduled to lapse with effect from which date?
explanation: The Budget 2026 documents clearly list that the notification providing exemptions for Naphtha (for fertilisers) and Silicon (for solar cells) will lapse with effect from 01.04.2026.

text: 59. Aligning with green energy roadmaps, Budget 2026 proposed an outlay of ₹20,000 crore over 5 years for CCUS technologies across industries like steel and cement. What does CCUS stand for?
explanation: CCUS stands for Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage. Budget 2026 proposed scaling up these technologies across five industrial sectors.

text: 60. To ease foreign investment and facilitate doing business, Budget 2026 increased the overall investment limit for all individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs) in the equity of listed Indian companies to:
explanation: Budget 2026 increased the individual PROI limit to 10%, and critically, it raised the overall aggregate investment limit for all individual PROIs from the current 10% to 24%.

text: 61. To bolster India's digital presence, Budget 2026 proposed setting up Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools for the 'AVGC' sector. What does AVGC stand for?

options.text: Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics

explanation: AVGC stands for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics. This growing industry is projected to require 2 million professionals by 2030, hence the creation of new labs.

text: 62. The 'White Revolution' in India was launched in 1970 to massively scale up the domestic production of which commodity?
explanation: The White Revolution (also known as Operation Flood) was led by Verghese Kurien and focused on drastically increasing milk production and creating the Amul cooperative model.

text: 63. In the categorization of Indian agricultural and industrial revolutions, the 'Black Revolution' is associated with an increase in the production of:
explanation: The Black Revolution relates to the self-sufficiency and increased production of Petroleum products.

text: 64. The 'Grey Revolution' is a term used to describe the rapid increase in the production of which essential industrial agricultural input?
explanation: The Grey Revolution specifically denotes the rapid increase in the production of Fertilizers in India.

text: 65. The 'Pink Revolution' is associated with the increased production and technological upgradation of which two specific items?
explanation: The Pink Revolution focuses on the production and export of Onions and Pharmaceuticals, as well as Prawns/Shrimp. (Red Revolution is for Meat and Tomatoes; Golden is for Fruits and Honey).

text: 66. Which Five-Year Plan in Indian history is broadly considered the 'most failed plan' due to severe economic strains caused by external aggressions (wars) and internal drought crises?
explanation: The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966) failed to meet its target largely because of the Sino-Indian War (1962), the Indo-Pak War (1965), and a severe drought.

text: 67. Following the massive failure of the Third Five-Year Plan, the government implemented a 'Plan Holiday' from 1966 to 1969. During this period, the focus was shifted primarily toward:

options.text: Rapid industrialization of the Defense sector
A 'New Agriculture Strategy' or 'Green Revolution' with HYV seeds

explanation: During the Plan Holiday (1966-1969), annual plans were made and the primary focus was shifted to combating the food crisis by introducing the 'New Agriculture Strategy' involving High-Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds—the dawn of the Green Revolution.

text: 68. Under the Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) of 1956, how did the government primarily incentivize the opening of new industries in economically backward areas to counter regional disparities?

options.text: By completely abolishing income tax for all employees in those areas.
By offering easy licensing and subsidization of critical inputs like electricity and water.
By forcing private companies to relocate.
By giving out free land without any regulatory oversight.

explanation: The government aimed to balance regional development by making it easier to obtain industrial licenses in backward areas and by subsidizing essential inputs like electricity and water.

text: 69. According to Schedule A of the IPR 1956, which of the following industries was designated as an exclusive monopoly of the State?
explanation: Schedule A consisted of 17 strategic industries exclusively reserved for the State. This included atomic energy, arms and ammunition, iron and steel, and the Indian Railways.

text: 70. Which of the following industries was placed under Schedule B of the IPR 1956, wherein the State would establish new undertakings but private enterprise was expected to supplement the effort?
explanation: Aluminium, machine tools, sea transport, and fertilizers were part of the 12 industries listed in Schedule B. Shipbuilding, aircraft, and electricity generation were under Schedule A.

text: 71. Which environmental process, heavily promoted in industrial contexts to mitigate climate change, is defined as the capturing and storing of atmospheric carbon dioxide?
explanation: Carbon sequestration is the process of capturing and storing atmospheric CO2 to reduce its concentration. This directly links to the CCUS (Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage) funding in the latest Budget.

text: 72. Biogas, which is utilized heavily for domestic consumption and rural industrialization via Gobar gas plants, is primarily composed of which two gases?
explanation: Generated through anaerobic digestion, Biogas is primarily composed of Methane (CH4) at 55-70% and Carbon Dioxide (CO2) at 30-40%.

text: 73. Geothermal energy is the heat and electricity produced from the interior of the Earth. Where are the two primary experimental geothermal projects located in India?

options.text: Parvati Valley (Manikaran, Himachal Pradesh) and Puga Valley (Ladakh)

explanation: India has set up two experimental projects to harness geothermal energy: one in the Parvati valley near Manikaran in Himachal Pradesh, and the other in the Puga Valley of Ladakh.

text: 74. The headquarters of the Second Green Revolution (SGR) cell, focused on holistic agricultural development and expanding HYV technology, is located at:
explanation: The headquarters of the Second Green Revolution (SGR) cell is located at the ICAR-RCER (Indian Council of Agricultural Research-Research Complex for Eastern Region) in Patna, Bihar.

text: 75. In a major move for 'Ease of Doing Business' in Budget 2026, approvals required for cargo clearance (including food, drugs, and wildlife products) will be seamlessly processed through a single digital window by which target date?
explanation: Budget 2026 declared that processes involved in the clearance of food, drugs, plant, animal, and wildlife products will be operationalised on a single interconnected digital window by April 2026 itself.

text: 36. While the Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measure inflation and prices, which statistical indicator is used to measure the volume and growth of industrial production in India?
explanation: The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) measures the growth or volume of industrial production (Manufacturing, Mining, Electricity) over a specific period, acting as a gauge for the health of the industrial sector.

text: 37. Which government body is officially responsible for compiling and publishing the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India?

options.text: Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP)

explanation: The IIP is published by the National Statistical Organisation (NSO), which operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

text: 38. What is the current 'Base Year' utilized for calculating the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India?
explanation: The current base year for calculating the IIP is 2011-2012, though discussions are ongoing to update it to a more recent year like 2022-23.

text: 39. Established in 1955, the Karve Committee played a foundational role in India's industrial planning. What was the primary focus of this committee?
explanation: The Karve Committee (1955) was set up to promote rural development and employment through village and small-scale industries alongside the heavy industrialization of the Second Five-Year Plan.

text: 40. In standard economic development models, a country usually transitions from the Primary sector to the Secondary sector, and finally to the Tertiary sector. What was unique about India's developmental path?

options.text: India remained entirely in the Primary sector.
India jumped directly to the Tertiary (service) sector, skipping a strong, full industrialization phase (Secondary sector).
India developed the Secondary sector completely before moving back to the Primary sector.
India skipped the Primary sector entirely.

explanation: Unlike industrialized nations like China, India's economy uniquely leaped from an agrarian base directly to a service-oriented economy, largely skipping widespread industrialization and the robust development of the Secondary Sector.

text: 41. Workers engaged in the Secondary Sector, which involves transforming raw materials into valuable manufactured products, are conventionally classified as:
explanation: The Secondary Sector includes manufacturing, construction, and processing. Workers in these heavy labor and factory environments are traditionally referred to as 'Blue Collar' workers.

text: 42. The e-Shram portal was launched by the Indian Government to create a comprehensive national database of which specific demographic?
explanation: The e-Shram portal is a major initiative aimed at registering and securing the welfare of unorganized sector workers (like construction workers, street vendors, and domestic helpers) across India.

text: 43. Which of the following is NOT recognized as a Major Industrial Region in India?
explanation: The Major Industrial Regions in India include the Mumbai-Pune belt, Hugli belt, Bangalore-Tamil Nadu belt, Gujarat region, Chota Nagpur plateau, Vishakhapatnam-Guntur belt, Gurgaon-Delhi-Meerut belt, and Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram. The Thar Desert Corridor is not one of them.

text: 44. To build upon the semiconductor sector capabilities, the Union Budget 2026 proposed launching 'ISM 2.0'. What does ISM stand for?
explanation: ISM stands for India Semiconductor Mission. Budget 2026 launched ISM 2.0 to produce equipment and materials and design full-stack Indian IP to fortify supply chains.

text: 45. To capitalize on the manufacturing momentum, Budget 2026 proposed increasing the financial outlay for the 'Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme' to:
explanation: Launched initially with ₹22,919 crore, the outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme was significantly increased to ₹40,000 crore in the 2026 Budget.

text: 46. The Union Budget 2026 proposed establishing dedicated 'Rare Earth Corridors' to promote mining and processing. Which state is NOT included in this specific plan?
explanation: The Budget explicitly identified Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu to establish dedicated Rare Earth Corridors. Karnataka is not part of this specific list.

text: 47. To reduce import dependency and boost domestic production, Budget 2026 proposed supporting States in establishing dedicated Chemical Parks through a plug-and-play model. How many such Chemical Parks are planned?
explanation: The 2026 Budget announced a scheme to support States in establishing exactly 3 dedicated Chemical Parks.

text: 48. Which new scheme was introduced in Budget 2026 to strengthen the domestic manufacturing of technologically advanced items like lifts, fire-fighting equipment, and tunnel-boring machines?

options.text: Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE)

explanation: The Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) was explicitly introduced to boost domestic manufacturing of high-value equipment like tunnel-boring machines and multi-story lifts.

text: 49. In order to create a globally competitive logistics ecosystem, Budget 2026 allocated ₹10,000 crore over a 5-year period for which specific manufacturing scheme?
explanation: A budgetary allocation of ₹10,000 crore over 5 years was proposed for the Scheme for Container Manufacturing.

text: 50. For the labour-intensive Textile Sector, Budget 2026 proposed an Integrated Programme. How many sub-parts does this overarching textile programme have?
explanation: The Integrated Programme for the Textile Sector consists of 5 sub-parts (National Fibre Scheme, Textile Expansion, Handloom programme, Tex-Eco Initiative, and Samarth 2.0).

text: 51. Under the 5-part Integrated Textile Programme of Budget 2026, which scheme aims for self-reliance in natural fibres (like silk and jute) and new-age fibres?
explanation: The National Fibre Scheme is designed specifically to ensure self-reliance in the production of natural, man-made, and new-age fibres.

text: 52. Which sub-part of the Budget 2026 Textile Programme specifically focuses on modernizing and upgrading the textile skilling ecosystem through collaboration with academic institutions?
explanation: Samarth 2.0 is the specific sub-part of the textile programme designed to modernize the textile skilling ecosystem in collaboration with industry and academia.

text: 53. In Budget 2026, to improve cost competitiveness and efficiency through infrastructure and technology upgradation, the government proposed a scheme to revive how many 'legacy industrial clusters'?
explanation: The government proposed to introduce a scheme aimed at rejuvenating and reviving 200 legacy industrial clusters.

text: 54. Recognising MSMEs as a vital engine of growth, Budget 2026 introduced an equity support initiative called the 'SME Growth Fund'. What is the dedicated corpus for this fund?
explanation: A dedicated ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund was introduced to provide equity support and create future 'Champions' out of micro and small enterprises.

text: 55. To promote environmentally sustainable movement of cargo, Budget 2026 proposed establishing a new Dedicated Freight Corridor connecting which two major locations?

options.text: Dankuni in the East, to Surat in the West

explanation: Budget 2026 explicitly proposed the establishment of a new Dedicated Freight Corridor connecting Dankuni in the East to Surat in the West.

text: 56. The 'Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme' launched in Budget 2026 aims to incentivize a modal shift from rail and road to inland waterways. What is the target percentage share for coastal shipping by the year 2047?
explanation: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme targets increasing the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping in logistics from the current 6% to 12% by the year 2047.

text: 57. To address global trade disruptions affecting manufacturing units in Special Economic Zones (SEZs), Budget 2026 introduced a one-time measure allowing them to sell goods to which area at concessional duty rates?
explanation: As a special one-time measure, Budget 2026 allowed eligible manufacturing units in SEZs to sell goods to the Domestic Tariff Area (DTA) at concessional rates of duty, limited to a prescribed proportion of their exports.

text: 58. According to the Customs Tariff notifications in Budget 2026, the basic customs duty exemption on 'Naphtha, for use in the manufacture of fertilisers' is scheduled to lapse with effect from which date?
explanation: The Budget 2026 documents clearly list that the notification providing exemptions for Naphtha (for fertilisers) and Silicon (for solar cells) will lapse with effect from 01.04.2026.

text: 59. Aligning with green energy roadmaps, Budget 2026 proposed an outlay of ₹20,000 crore over 5 years for CCUS technologies across industries like steel and cement. What does CCUS stand for?
explanation: CCUS stands for Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage. Budget 2026 proposed scaling up these technologies across five industrial sectors.

text: 60. To ease foreign investment and facilitate doing business, Budget 2026 increased the overall investment limit for all individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs) in the equity of listed Indian companies to:
explanation: Budget 2026 increased the individual PROI limit to 10%, and critically, it raised the overall aggregate investment limit for all individual PROIs from the current 10% to 24%.

text: 61. To bolster India's digital presence, Budget 2026 proposed setting up Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools for the 'AVGC' sector. What does AVGC stand for?

options.text: Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics

explanation: AVGC stands for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics. This growing industry is projected to require 2 million professionals by 2030, hence the creation of new labs.

text: 62. The 'White Revolution' in India was launched in 1970 to massively scale up the domestic production of which commodity?
explanation: The White Revolution (also known as Operation Flood) was led by Verghese Kurien and focused on drastically increasing milk production and creating the Amul cooperative model.

text: 63. In the categorization of Indian agricultural and industrial revolutions, the 'Black Revolution' is associated with an increase in the production of:
explanation: The Black Revolution relates to the self-sufficiency and increased production of Petroleum products.

text: 64. The 'Grey Revolution' is a term used to describe the rapid increase in the production of which essential industrial agricultural input?
explanation: The Grey Revolution specifically denotes the rapid increase in the production of Fertilizers in India.

text: 65. The 'Pink Revolution' is associated with the increased production and technological upgradation of which two specific items?
explanation: The Pink Revolution focuses on the production and export of Onions and Pharmaceuticals, as well as Prawns/Shrimp. (Red Revolution is for Meat and Tomatoes; Golden is for Fruits and Honey).
